name: Wallbox N.V.

profile.description: Wallbox is a Barcelona-based maker of electric vehicle charging hardware and software, including the Pulsar Plus home AC charger, the Quasar bidirectional DC charger, the Supernova and Hypernova public DC fast chargers, the myWallbox management platform and the Electromaps e-mobility app. In 2026 the company went through a court-supervised debt restructuring after entering Spanish pre-insolvency proceedings over about EUR 170M of bank liabilities, extending maturities to 2030 and raising new equity. Q2 2026 revenue was about EUR 23.9M, down 19% sequentially, with Q3 guided to EUR 29-31M. The NYSE has granted an 18-month cure period to regain compliance with listing standards. Market cap approximately $63M.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Wallbox expanded from home AC chargers (Pulsar Plus) into bidirectional DC home charging (Quasar) and public DC fast charging (Supernova, Hypernova), plus the Electromaps software platform. This opened a new public-charging revenue stream, though revenue has since fallen from EUR 164M in 2024 to EUR 139M in 2025 [1][2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI savings were found. Market Share (1/2): Wallbox is a meaningful European residential and DC charger player, but not a leader, and revenue is shrinking [2][3]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management points to the Quasar 2 and next-gen Supernova series, but without dated launches or revenue visibility [4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2024 R&D was EUR 15.5M on EUR 164.0M of revenue (~9.4%), above electrical-equipment peers [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Wallbox aims to change the way the world uses energy through smart EV charging and energy management, a clear purpose tied to electrification but not distinctive among charging peers [1][5]. Community Impact (0/2): Beyond a 2022 ESG report, no charitable or community programs were found [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): Wallbox entered pre-insolvency proceedings in March 2026, restructured its debt and renegotiated vendor terms, and replaced its CFO in December 2025, so this is not an environment that retains people for the mission [3][7][8]. Insider Buying (0/2): As a foreign private issuer, Wallbox insiders do not file US Form 4s, and no evidence of insider buying was found.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR APPLIED: average daily volume of about 14,263 shares (yfinance) at $2.67 equals roughly $38,000 a day; even FMP's higher 172,067-share average gives only ~$459,000, both below the $1,000,000 threshold, so Infrastructure = 0 [9][10]. The underlying metrics are also weak: YoY revenue growth of -37.5%, a profit margin of -94%, a negative forward P/E (-1.0), and negative book equity on FMP's TTM data before the 2026 restructuring [9][11]. Debt-to-equity and ROE are set to null because equity was negative before the restructuring and reported post-restructuring figures conflict. The 5-year revenue CAGR is null because FY2020 is reported in USD and later years in EUR.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Wallbox designs and manufactures physical EV charging hardware that must be installed on site and certified for electrical safety. AI cannot substitute for that, and no analyst commentary found flags AI as a risk; Wallbox's threats are EV adoption rates, competition and its balance sheet [3][12]. Software layers such as myWallbox and Electromaps could face AI-native energy-management competitors, but they are a small share of revenue. AI Opportunity (0/1): Wallbox reports no AI-related revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Wallbox began with an infinite-sounding ambition — changing how the world uses energy — but it is now in survival mode. The 2026 pre-insolvency process, debt restructuring and NYSE listing cure period mean every decision is about the next quarter's liquidity. The founder CEO's motto, 'if we want to be number one, we have to be the fastest', is a finite-game framing in Sinek's terms.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Accelerating the shift to electric mobility and smarter energy use has the idealistic shape Sinek describes, but Wallbox's strategy is now driven by restructuring and liquidity rather than by that cause, and the cause has not been tested through multiple cycles [1][3][7].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Pre-insolvency proceedings over about EUR 170M of liabilities, a 2026 restructuring signed with creditors holding ~83% of debt, operational constraints from vendor renegotiations and a CFO change in December 2025 all point to organizational instability rather than a Circle of Safety [3][7][8].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): CEO Enric Asunción frames the strategy as a race — 'If we want to be number one, we have to be the fastest' — which is the finite language of winning rather than learning from rivals [13].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Wallbox has moved from residential AC charging into bidirectional DC, public DC fast charging and energy management software, a meaningful expansion of its model [1][2]. These are adjacent moves within EV charging rather than a reinvention, and the 2026 restructuring was driven by necessity.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Leadership's recent decisions — pre-insolvency filing, debt restructuring and dilutive equity raises — are defensive survival actions. No evidence was found of costly long-term investments made from a position of strength [3][7].

investment_thesis: The bull case is that the 2026 restructuring resets Wallbox's capital structure: maturities were extended to December 2030, creditors holding about 83% of financial debt signed on, and new equity was raised. Order intake rose 11% sequentially in Q2 2026, building a backlog of nearly EUR 12M, and management guided Q3 revenue to EUR 29-31M with 38-40% gross margins as vendor constraints ease [3][4]. Wallbox's product range across home, bidirectional and public DC charging gives it exposure to any recovery in European EV adoption [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is severe. Revenue fell from EUR 164M in 2024 to EUR 139M in 2025 and is down further in 2026, the TTM net margin is about -94%, cash was only about EUR 20M at June 30, 2026, and the company needed pre-insolvency protection [2][3][7][11]. Average daily trading of well under $1M makes the stock untradeable for IOWN, the NYSE listing depends on an 18-month cure period, and further dilution is likely if the Q3 recovery does not materialize [3][9].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 revenue landing within the EUR 29-31M guidance as vendor terms normalize and the ~EUR 12M order backlog converts
Completion and court approval of the debt restructuring with maturities extended to 2030
A recovery in European EV sales and uptake of bidirectional (Quasar) and public DC (Supernova) charging
key_risks: Liquidity and solvency risk: ~EUR 20M of cash against ~EUR 140M of non-current debt after the restructuring
NYSE delisting risk if listing standards are not regained within the 18-month cure period
Further dilution and continued revenue declines as slow European EV adoption and charger competition pressure volumes and pricing

backlog.note: Wallbox disclosed an order backlog of nearly EUR 12M at end of Q2 2026 (amount in EUR) after order intake rose 11% sequentially while shipments lagged because of vendor renegotiations during the restructuring. No TTM book-to-bill is disclosed; a single quarter of orders above invoicing is too noisy to rate green. The backlog covers only about half a quarter of revenue, so visibility is low.
